string_literals: {=1IEroJKs}Not everyone who musters for the levy marches to war, and not everyone who goes on campaign sees action. You did both, and you also took down an enemy warrior in direct one-to-one combat, in the full view of your comrades.

{=4f5xwzX0}When your community needed to organize a posse to pursue horse thieves, you were the obvious choice. You hunted down the raiders, surrounded them and forced their surrender, and took back your stolen property.

{=DjeAJtix}Maybe it was a love affair, or maybe you cheated at dice, or maybe you just chose your words poorly when drinking with a dangerous crowd. Anyway, on one of your trips into town you got into the kind of trouble from which only a quick tongue or quick feet get you out alive.

{=FhZPjhli}Your hometown was briefly placed under siege, and you were called to defend the walls. Everyone did their part to repulse the enemy assault, and everyone is justly proud of what they endured.

{=I3PcdaaL}Wolves, bears are a constant menace to the flocks of northern Calradia, while hyenas and leopards trouble the south. You went with a group of your fellow villagers and fired the missile that brought down the beast.

{=PyVqDLBu}Your parents didn't give you much money, but they did leave just enough for you to secure a loan against a larger amount to build a small workshop. You paid back what you borrowed, and sold your enterprise for a profit.

{=ZAGR6PYc}When a sudden blaze broke out in a back alley, your neighbors needed quick-thinking leadership and you provided it. You organized a bucket line to the nearest well, putting the fire out before any homes were lost.
{=bWlmGDf3}When a sudden storm caused the local stream to rise suddenly, your neighbors needed quick-thinking leadership. You provided it, directing them to build levees to save their homes.

{=cbF9jdQo}Your parents didn't give you much money, but they did leave just enough for you to purchase a plot of unused land at the edge of the village. You cleared away rocks and dug an irrigation ditch, raised a few seasons of crops, than sold it for a considerable profit.

{=dDmcqTzb}Yours wasn't the kind of reputation that local legends are made of, but it was the kind that wins you respect among those around you. You were consistently fair and honest in your business dealings and helpful to those in trouble. In doing so, you got a sense of what made people tick.

string_literals: {=1SUTcF0J}The gang leaders who kept watch over the slums of Calradian cities were always in need of poor youth to run messages and back them up in turf wars, while thrill-seeking merchants' sons and daughters sometimes slummed it in their company as well.
{=6LFj919J}You helped dig wells, rethatch houses, and fix broken plows. You learned about the basics of construction, as well as what it takes to keep a farming community prosperous.
{=9ks4u5cH}You were sent by the village healer up into the hills to look for useful medicinal plants. You learned which herbs healed wounds or brought down a fever, and how to find them.
{=DIgsfYfz}You took your family's goods to the nearest town to sell your produce and buy supplies. It was hard work, but you enjoyed the hubbub of the marketplace.

{=Ghz90npw}Your family owned a few horses at the town stables and you took charge of their care. Many evenings you would take them out beyond the walls and gallup through the fields, racing other youth.

{=KfaqPpbK}You went with other fleet-footed youths to take the villages' sheep, goats or cattle to graze in pastures near the village. You were in charge of chasing down stray beasts, and always kept a big stone on hand to be hurled at lurking predators if necessary.
{=RuvSk3QT}You accompanied a local hunter as he went into the wilderness, helping him set up traps and catch small animals.

{=bhdkegZ4}All towns had their share of projects that were constantly in need of both skilled and unskilled labor. You learned how hoists and scaffolds were constructed, how planks and stones were hewn and fitted, and other skills.
{=gAjvAGTa}hung out with the gangs in the alleys.

{=hXl25avg}Your family arranged for a private tutor and you took full advantage, reading voraciously on history, mathematics, and philosophy and discussing what you read with your tutor and classmates.
{=qnqdEJOv}You watched the town's watch practice shooting and perfect their plans to defend the walls in case of a siege.
{=rmMcwSn8}You helped your family handle their business affairs, going down to the marketplace to make purchases and oversee the arrival of caravans.
{=y6j1bJTH}You were apprenticed to the local smith. You learned how to heat and forge metal, hammering for hours at a time until your muscles ached.

string_literals: {=5QSGoRFj}Your family tilled one of the small patches of arable land in the steppes for generations. When the Khuzaits came, they ceased paying taxes to the emperor and providing conscripts for his army, and served the khan instead.

{=9aoQYpZs}Your family's clan never pledged its loyalty to the khan and never settled down, preferring to live out in the deep steppe away from his authority. They remain some of the finest trackers and scouts in the grasslands, as the ability to spot an enemy coming and move quickly is often all that protects their herds from their neighbors' predations.

{=URgZ4ai4}Your family were middle-ranking members of one of the Khuzait clans. He had some herds of his own, but was not rich. When the Khuzait horde was summoned to battle, he fought with the horse archers, shooting and wheeling and wearing down the enemy before the lancers delivered the final punch.

{=WOKNhaG2}Your family were guardians of the sacred traditions of the Khuzaits, channelling the spirits of the wilderness and of the ancestors. They tended the sick and dispensed wisdom, resolving disputes and providing practical advice.

{=jAs3kDXh}Your family were the trusted kinsfolk of a Khuzait noyan, and shared his meals in the chieftain's yurt. Your father assisted his chief in running the affairs of the clan and fought in the core of armored lancers in the center of the Khuzait battle line.

{=qPg3IDiq}Your family came from one of the merchant clans that dominated the cities in eastern Calradia before the Khuzait conquest. They adjusted quickly to their new masters, keeping the caravan routes running and ensuring that the tariff revenues that once went into imperial coffers now flowed to the khanate.

string_literals: {=1s3bHupn}You're not getting along with the rest of the company. It's better you go.
{=2g18dlwo}I would like to assign you a new role.
{=3bOcF1Cw}I can't spare anyone now. You will need to go alone.
{=5ajobQiL}What role do you have in mind?
{=6uUzWz46}I see. Maybe we will speak again when I have one.
{=7EoBCTX0}What do you want me to do?
{=8VlqJteC}I was just jesting. I need you more than ever. Now go back to your job.
{=92mngWSd}All right. It's good to be back.
{=ArNB7aaL}Where exactly did you have in mind?[if:convo_happy]
{=B9uT9wa6}I wish to reward you for your services.
{=BaeqKlQ6}I am not allowed to talk with you.
{=Dga7sQOu}I no longer need you as Surgeon.
{=DiEKuVGF}We'll make ready to set out at once.
{=E91oU7oi}I no longer need you as Engineer.
{=EUQnsZFb}I no longer need you as Scout.
{=GjpJN2xE}I no longer need you as Quartermaster.

{=IkH0pVhC}I would be honored, my {?PLAYER.GENDER}lady{?}lord{\?}. But I can't take on any new responsibilities while leading this caravan. If you wish to relieve me of my duties, we can discuss this further.
{=KqazzTWV}Indeed. You have shed your blood for me, and you deserve a fief of your own..
{=LDGMSQJJ}Very well. Let me think on this a bit longer
{=LOiZfCEy}My {?PLAYER.GENDER}lady{?}lord{\?}, it would be an honor if you were to choose the name of my noble house.
{=MDik3Kfn}I want you to recruit some troops.
{=Mt9abZzi}{SETTLEMENT_NAME}? This is a great honor, my {?PLAYER.GENDER}lady{?}lord{\?}. I will protect it until the last drop of my blood.[ib:hip][if:convo_happy]
{=OMaM6ihN}I want you to patrol the area.
{=Q0xPr6CP}I cannot be sure of your loyalty any longer.
{=SVEptNxR}It's only normal that you have second thoughts. I will be right by your side if you change your mind, my {?PLAYER.GENDER}lady{?}lord{\?}.[ib:hip][if:convo_nervous]

{=TXO1ihiZ}Thank you, my {?PLAYER.GENDER}lady{?}lord{\?}. I have often thought about that. If I had a fief, with revenues, and perhaps a title to go with it, I could marry well and pass my wealth down to my heirs, and of course raise troops to help defend the realm.
{=TtlwXnVc}I am pleased to grant you the title of {CULTURE_SPECIFIC_TITLE} and the fiefdom of {SETTLEMENT_NAME}.. You richly deserve it.
{=Wx5ysDp1}My {?PLAYER.GENDER}lady{?}lord{\?}, as much as I appreciate the gesture, I am not sure that you have a suitable estate to grant me.
{=Y6Z8qNW9}I'll need you to lead a party.
{=YyNywO6Z}Think nothing of it. I'm glad you're safe.
{=aCwCaWGC}Your skills are not what I need.
{=bUzU50P8}What? Why? Did I do something wrong?[ib:closed]
{=dRKk0E1V}Unfortunately, I can't take you back right now.
{=dpYhBgAC}Thank you my {?PLAYER.GENDER}lady{?}lord{\?}. I will always remember this grand gesture.[ib:hip][if:convo_happy]
{=drIfaTa7}Rejoin the others and let's be off.
{=gT2O4YXc}I will go off on my own, then. I can stay busy. But I'll remember - I owe you one!
{=i7k0AXsO}I see. We will speak again when you are relieved from your duty.
{=kAbebv72}I want you to go forage some food.
{=m3AsvplJ}I already have quite a few duties. Perhaps you could relieve me of one of them, so that I can take on this new responsibility?
{=o2g6Wi9K}As you wish. Will I take some troops with me?
{=pRsCnGoo}I no longer have need of your services.
{=sxc2D6NJ}I am thinking of a different location.
{=vctta154}Well {PLAYER.NAME}, it is certainly good to see you still retain your sense of humor.[if:convo_nervous][ib:normal2]
{=ywtuRAmP}Time has taken its toll on us all, friend. It's time that you retire.

string_literals: {=3O1Pg3Ie}At {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} 14th birthday you gave {CHILD.NAME} a special present. You have seen {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?} treasure it and believe it will shape who {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} is. You gave {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?}...
{=3hFT34l1}{?PLAYER_CHILD}Your{?}The{\?} child helps out the local physician, binding and cleaning wounds and, when the master is absent, prescribing remedies.
{=6WUaFzlv}{?PLAYER_CHILD}Your{?}The{\?} child forged a sword - blade, hilt and pommel. The artisan said that he has never seen such dedication and patience in one so young.
{=7JoiyH1Y}You heard that {CHILD.NAME} could put an arrow through an arm ring from 100 paces away, but you didn't believe it until you saw it.
{=7mbE4z2v}{?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} won a friendly horse racing competition, and was rewarded with a magnificent saddle.
{=AaahFmxv}War was never too far away. On more than one occasion, {CHILD.NAME} spotted foes on the horizon and needed to ride away as quickly as possible.

{=DfbYtRyj}You had second thoughts about giving {?PLAYER_CHILD}your{?}the{\?} child such a spirited animal, but {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} lept upon its back and galloped like the wind across your pastures.
{=GOt2uRcJ}In adolescence, {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} began to take on serious responsibilities and compete with adults as a near-equal. {?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} managed to...
{=K31F1yPI}When you pick up this blade you can almost feel it dance in your hand. Its edge can cut through a stout poll or a human hair drifting on the wind.

{=MX7toYav}{CHILD.NAME} joined a hunting pursuit in pursuit of a pack of wolves who had been ravaging the local livestock. {?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} tracked and took down one of the beasts with an arrow.
{=R7A3aPwi}A neighboring noble's brutish son took an interest in persecuting {CHILD.NAME}, but the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} gave him reason to look elsewhere for his prey.

{=S3RZLOsv}You can sense the power in the laminated sinews and wood of this weapon. It was made for the calloused hands of a veteran archer and {CHILD.NAME} may need years to be able to fully draw it back, but you know {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} will be motivated to master it.

{=bTj16PqR}Every well-born youth wants to see the center of it all, where the lords and ladies gather in splendor to converse and connive. You invited the child to see the spectacle first hand, and provided the elegant clothes {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?}'d need to be part of it.
{=cnbeJh6Y}After many tries {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} successfully beat {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} tutor, fair and square, during sparring.
{=cr2jmYxg}You remember poring over the hand-drawn schematics of mangonels and towers for hours, imagining that one day you might build one of these awesome instruments of destruction yourself.
{=fzxJZZEH}Each piece is a work of art. Even without an opponent one could set it up and gaze upon it for hours, contemplating moves and counter-moves.

{=jukOfT2Z}Outside events also intruded on {CHILD.NAME}'s adolescence. You believe {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} was particularly shaped by {RANDOM_OUTCOME}. This event increased {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} skills in {SKILL_1} and {SKILL_2}.
{=kAtxHSu9}A great illness swept through your lands. Your child applied what {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} had read in books on nursing fevers and isolating the sick to minimize deaths on your estate.
{=lDMrl7sd}Your district saw more than its share of floods and fires, and {CHILD.NAME} joined in the effort to stem the destruction and rebuild afterwards.

{=oaXAY8bw}{?PLAYER_CHILD}Your{?}The{\?} child asked to borrow money to trade with a passing caravan. You figure {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?}'d be sharped and learn a lesson, but in fact the {?CHILD.GENDER}girl{?}boy{\?} secured a very lucrative deal.
{=yym5kCG5}After a particularly hard winter your tenants began to murmur about rising up and seizing your granaries. {CHILD.NAME} convinced them to be patient and wait for relief.

IL_0631: ldstr          {=kAtxHSu9}A great illness swept through your lands. Your child applied what {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} had read in books on nursing fevers and isolating the sick to minimize deaths on your estate.
IL_065e: ldstr          {=Jc1YXXjN}an influx of wild beasts

IL_0669: ldstr          {=MX7toYav}{CHILD.NAME} joined a hunting pursuit in pursuit of a pack of wolves who had been ravaging the local livestock. {?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} tracked and took down one of the beasts with an arrow.

IL_06a1: ldstr          {=yym5kCG5}After a particularly hard winter your tenants began to murmur about rising up and seizing your granaries. {CHILD.NAME} convinced them to be patient and wait for relief.

string_literals: {=0XOii9tg}The noble did not let {CHILD.NAME} go hand-to-hand with other warriors, but the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} joined the archers as they traded shots with enemy scouts.

{=1NCVDNri}The noble gave the young adult command of a small group of scouts. {?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} took them on patrol and even though some were twice {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} age, {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} won their respect.
{=1vQul57Y}The caravan got lost and it was {CHILD.NAME} who spotted the landmarks that got it back on track.
{=2EOvlPc2}Gripped by wanderlust, {?PLAYER_CHILD}your{?}the{\?} child rode from the freezing woods of Sturgia to the blazing Nahasa.
{=3ZZtAYXm}The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} learned to treat the mangled fingers and concussions without which no siege is complete.
{=4CuMDzvd}You asked your best warrior to take {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?} under his wings and make sure {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} gets the taste of battle without being seriously harmed.
{=4nUhnWZ3}There was a great deal of feasting and speech-making. From what you hear, {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} acquitted {?CHILD.GENDER}herself{?}himself{\?} well.
{=53xrtZst}Before {CHILD.NAME} left, you asked the lord to make sure that the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?}...
{=5vosR2YO}The host was the kind of man who likes to do his negotiations from the saddle in pursuit of deer, and {CHILD.NAME} joined in every expedition.
{=6q8tY6Sz}You remember your freebooting days fondly. You want {CHILD.NAME} to experience life as you did.
{=7hYUleHh}rode to the edge of the world.

{=8AjlID6z}You hear talk of incriminating letters and loose tongues paid to stay silent. You're not sure exactly what happened, but {?PLAYER_CHILD}your{?}the{\?} child seems more worldly than {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} did when {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} left.
{=8alDLq0s}not to be too choosy about travelling companions.
{=9BoHka98}The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} pursued enemy scouts while avoiding their main force. There was little fighting but a great deal of riding.
{=CpcWqufH}The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} was placed in command of a small group of militiamen, including some nearly twice {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} age, and earned their respect.
{=DOhOpmhV}You found {CHILD.NAME} an apprenticeship with a siege engineer. Even if it can be a bit dangerous, there's no substitute for that kind of practical experience.
{=ETfx08db}see as much of the world as {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} could.
{=EXwX0zrx}The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} faced a rival clan's outrider in single combat, and handed him a defeat that he wouldn't forget.
{=FekWDIUm}{?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} helped plan a small expedition in pursuit of a group of brigands.
{=Fn7Pgia7}{?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} told you that {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} skill with a lance paid for much of {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} journey.
{=K1HrvDLO}{?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} won't talk much about it, but you know that {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} has seen the darker side of Calradia.
{=KB0fv5Me}The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} charmed {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} way into a circle of nobles and was a welcome guest at well-set tables.
{=KgJaq5dx}You sent the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} to the hall of one of your fellow lords. There {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} will learn how a different clan runs its affairs.
{=La7wkS5M}The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} defeated several opponents and did honor to your clan's name.
{=MUaFiBva}{CHILD.NAME} paid close attention to the experienced engineers and became competent in a profession where small mistakes can have deadly consequences.
{=Q39oLjSu}One of the entourage was thrown from a horse on the road. The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} set the broken bone and ensured it healed cleanly.
{=TaAHFZfd}You asked your head of expedition to make sure that your {?CHILD.GENDER}daughter{?}son{\?}...
{=U9nsz7pg}Before {CHILD.NAME} left, you asked the siege engineer to make sure that the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?}...
{=UGda4FDZ}{CHILD.NAME} found work with an artisan for a season, keeping {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} high birth a secret.
{=UYdvhdDl}When cargo went missing, the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} made the inquiries at the local black market that were necessary to get it back.
{=V0QmrGda}Before {CHILD.NAME} left, you asked your warrior to make sure that the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?}...

{=VTzvlEV8}Sparring with total strangers, including some who would happily break {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} teeth if {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} let them, was a new and valuable experience for {CHILD.NAME}.
{=VVBx07cK}The siege engines needed gears and bracings, and the master assigned {?PLAYER_CHILD}your{?}the{\?} child to assist in forging them.
{=WD6soDM1}It was a minor skirmish but a clear victory nonetheless. {CHILD.NAME} wasn't just there when the commander came up with the winning strategy but also took part in executing it.
{=WJSapWab}{?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} had a chance to fight in a few minor skirmishes without getting seriously injured.
{=WL1zcgYx}{?CHILD.GENDER}She{?}He{\?} travelled on foot in the company of other pilgrims, often relying on the kindness of strangers for food and shelter.

{=Yk3xrawy}When {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} returns, {CHILD.NAME} tells you the story of how {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} {RANDOM_OUTCOME} That event increased {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} skill in {SKILL}.
{=aCMZafK5}The fight was over a minor insult, and only to the first blood. But you're still relieved that the first blood in question belonged to the other youth.
{=aCO0Md8z}When {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} was ambused on patrol, {CHILD.NAME} fought the attackers off with sheer willpower.
{=bCZbgrLU}The smith came down sick and the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} had to quickly learn how to craft horseshoes and nails.
{=cDVNFn4p}Before {CHILD.NAME} left, you told the merchant that {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} should be entrusted with...
{=cyQXm7VA}The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} was charged with ensuring they had the food, saddles, animals, teamsters and guards for the journey.
{=egXc7J72}Caravan guards are not elite troops, and may slack off if not held to a high standard of discipline. {CHILD.NAME} made sure that they stayed sober and alert.
{=fsr2yhrr}While there were few military feats to accomplish, {CHILD.NAME} still became quite popular among the troops and improved their morale in the process.

{=hjOxidJj}The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} will spend {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} time at a diplomatic mission, where {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} will have chance to interact with people from foreign lands.

{=igkNYcSI}The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} tells you how engineers have become an unofficial guild that transcends borders. Even men on opposite sides of a siege are known to discuss the technical details of their craft.
{=ijootCu7}It was easy to get bogged down in the details of hurling rocks and assembling towers, but {CHILD.NAME} kept a keen eye on why some sieges succeeded and others failed.
{=oCiWOutS}Sieges required tools, oil, good quality timber and, of course, food. It was young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?}'s responsibility to have them gathered, stocked and distributed.
{=rVIzHhLO}The young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?}'s social graces helped put other merchants at ease as they exchanged information and worked out deals.
{=rZkQfBxt}You asked one of the local merchants to take the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} along with one of his caravans and make {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?} learn the secrets of the trade.
{=taKIDPxj}Embassies carry gifts and attract bandits. Fighting them off made the trip much more exciting than {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} had expected.
{=yJ0XRD9g}Eventually it was time for {?PLAYER_CHILD}your{?}the{\?} child to travel far from home. You sent the young {?CHILD.GENDER}woman{?}man{\?} away...

string_literals: {=1oPRugXl}Trick knife throws and swift evasions can entertain a marketplace crowd, but are useful on the battlefield as well.
{=3iED3Ca9}To craft a tactic one must first have an idea of what has worked in the past and what has failed, and any commander should know the course and outcome of as many battles as possible.
{=5pGCtBhd}You asked that your child be schooled over the next few years in all the treatises that can be found on human body, its ailments, and their treatments.
{=6apaXF8k}You wanted this child to learn most from those who worked with their hands for a living. You asked an artisan in your employ to teach {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?}...
{=9m5M3Yf9}Some nobles may consider it vulgar and common, but the art of acrobatics is demanding and often has very practical applications.

{=9sdTLp49}The master artisan supervises the work of any smiths, carpenters or masons that you hire. {?PLAYER_CHILD}Your{?}The{\?} child will join in the hard work and learn both stamina and craftsmanship.
{=Adah5bay}The most powerful weapons require years of practice and conditioning to use properly. Their wielders need to start early.
{=BTdTSzxF}You felt that your child should learn first and foremost how to manage the family property and govern your retainers.
{=C5UrdSgj}Fast legs and stamina are as vital to a warrior's survival as {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} strength and skill.
{=CZuYne8X}Singing, dancing and playing an instrument is important but the {?IS_BATTANIA}bard{?}minstrel{\?} knows more. You asked him to make sure the child is also skilled in...

{=CtImGA4A}Most tutors teach mathematics from tracing the path of stars in the sky, but you wanted your {?IS_BATTANIA_OR_KHUZAIT}lorekeeper{?}scholar{\?} to focus on the more practical architectural treatises.
{=EbRDo6Lv}A hunter should be able to endure long treks over rough ground and pursue a wounded quarry until it drops.

{=G7yjkafk}The lorekeeper is responsible for teaching children the ancestral knowledge of the clan, including genealogy, law, and medicine. {?PLAYER_CHILD}Your{?}The{\?} child should gain a respect for learning.
{=GvSVxyO0}Your steward is happy with the child's progress. He informs you that {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} shows some natural talent in {SKILL}.
{=Ir7BP5bD}The best smiths are those that understand how their tools are used. Your child will be tasked with sparring with the weapons and testing their edges.
{=ItS9F61H}You told {CHILD.NAME} that any young noble worth {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}his{\?} salt should be able to bring down a deer from fifty paces away, or hit a rabbit on the run.
{=JGEQ68jc}Your huntsman is happy with the child's progress. He informs you that {?CHILD.GENDER}she{?}he{\?} shows some natural talent in {SKILL}.

{=K08ed2LS}You asked your master-at-arms to make sure that as a noble, this {?CHILD.GENDER}daughter{?}son{\?} of the clan knows how to hold {?CHILD.GENDER}herself{?}himself{\?} properly on the saddle.
{=KC7rLf4b}The {?IS_BATTANIA}bard{?}minstrel{\?} had the child memorize the speeches of epic heroes, teaching {?CHILD.GENDER}her{?}him{\?} how to appeal to your people's pride in their ancestors.

string_literals: {=0CCgjMTG}Cover the bodies as best you can and hope for the best

{=0DSopB7F}After observing the terrain around {FORTRESS_NAME}, you think conditions might be appropriate for mining - digging a tunnel under a wall, then collapsing it. This can open a breach but is time-consuming and risky. If you encounter rock underground, you may find all your efforts go to waste. If the ground is too soft, the tunnel may collapse and bury your men. Most troops are reluctant to spend time in dark, confined tunnels unless they are paid extra, or forced.
{=0Wwwa77J}Tell the trader that you have no wish to profit from his ignorance
{=0ZP5fDBX}Let the wealthier merchant know that your decision is for sale.
{=0awbcZag}Give him your blessing and encourage him to bore everyone to tears with his old war stories.
{=0k4T7dzu}Return the rooster and have your man whipped.
{=0lqAKHfU}Tell your men to be forgiving, as they were once recruits themselves
{=0wRiev5G}Show genuine remorse and participate in the burial rites for the deer, just in case, even if your troops make comments behind your back
{=0xiAZr96}Tell {NOBLE.NAME} that your people will get their reeds elsewhere and stop frightening off the game.
{=12bIzNkB}Tell him that no one sells maps to treasures that they could just as easily dig up themselves
{=1b9oYu6v}Tell them they can join you and be as arrogant as they like - so long as they beat one of your men in a duel to first blood.
{=1bobtmxl}Sell him your cheapest horse so that he can continue.

{=1jAyaivZ}As you pass through the village streets, a dog dashes out from among some spectators and bites at the heels of one of your {CAVALRYMAN}'s horses, panicking it. The mount rears and gallops down the street, trampling a vegetable vendor who was unable to get out of its way. She will probably walk with a limp hereafter, and her family demands compensation.
{=1zsWhG2N}Tell your men as best you can that, while you respect their spirit, this will frighten local farmers who don't understand warriors' ways.
{=24pUil64}You like that fiery spirit! Let them fight until one falls and cannot rise
{=2GMj6ZaW}Carry the bodies with you until you find dry wood or softer ground

{=2KaXj3Qa}The depredations of the {NEARBY_ENEMY_FACTION} has driven many farmers from their homes. Those who have land usually return to it, but many of the poorer are seeking a new place to live. You speak to a few encamped on the outskirts of your village. There is no land for them. They seem eager to work as tenants, but there is always a possibility of tensions with the more established village families.

{=2OQlwt7x}Villagers say that a wanderer has recently arrived and offered to teach their children to read. He is not only well-educated, but he has a gift for holding the attention of restless 10-year-olds. However, he seems to have spent time with one of the rebel bands that were common around here ten years back, and occasionally speaks of a coming reign of justice brought by Heaven, in a way that doesn't seem like one of his ironic jokes.
{=2auYPXJ8}Declare that you owe your victory to your own right arm, and keep the silver
{=2dW3cBQy}That steel is forged from iron, and long hard marches breed tough warriors.
{=2xvqOUJh}Tell him quietly that you will not profit off of the misery of others.
{=37YTPzfG}Tell your men that they have all earned the right to your esteem, and break out an extra ration of {FOOD_OR_DRINK_ITEM} to show your appreciation
{=37lEhqtv}Let them fight until the first drop of blood is shed
{=3CaDxb8R}Remind your men that war is war, the {TROOP_TYPE} knew the risks, and prisoners bring ransoms

{=3FwbFdbw}As you inspect your siege camp, you come across disgusting evidence that one or more of your men has contracted the bloody flux. It will pass from man to man as they share food and water, and you know what it can do to a besieging army if left unchecked.

{=3IphvZTK}In your absence, several families in your district have been hard at work draining a marsh and turning it into a field. The survey records in your treasury however indicate clearly that the marsh is part of your domain. They almost certainly did not know this, but you are entitled to claim the field or charge them for working it.
{=3OerG5Ik}Take the teacher aside, and tell him the elder will pay him a handsome stipend that will stop abruptly if he breathes a word about politics or theology.
{=3QobDImA}Help them get back on their feet, even if some will call say that you are too trusting
{=3Uub2e17}Tell your men that there shall be no wine tonight, and none henceforth until they learn how to handle themselves in the desert.
{=3WFuf7OC}Give them money to purchase land near your fief in {VILLAGE_NAME}, so long as they take charge of training the local militia.

{=3eOOT66E}One of your tenants has a proposal for you. He proposes to dig a channel known as a qanah into a hillside, where the water table is high, which will allow him to flood some low-lying ground and turn it into an oasis garden. The barren hillside is your property, though at present it yields no income of any kind.
{=3uHIXyDk}Your men could use a laugh. Let the recruit show off his prize to his mates and take the humiliation, even if it's enough to drive him to desert
{=3zEtGAII}You agree with the ancient Palaic principle: the lands belong to the spirits of the earth, not to humans, and go to those who make the best use of them.
{=3zP80NBJ}Tell them that village disputes are a matter for a proper inquest by the authorities

{=42bGMh4X}Your men were not expecting to spend so much time in the desert. They complain that baggage that they might gladly carry themselves in normal times becomes a crushing burden when the blazing sun is high in the sky. They have located a number of pack animals in the markets and ask you to buy them to lighten their own loads.
{=43GeTG0K}Accept, even if it costs you time, recognizing that a warrior who survived so many battles probably knows a thing or two.
{=47hUs9yg}You make an example of the foreman. You hand him over to the town authorities and encourage them to apply the full penalty - branding as a thief and exile from the town.
{=4Ef7xG1o}Propitiate the spirits as the villagers advised, by slaughtering a black cockerel that they sold one of your men.
{=4WZ5CWm8}Take them aside and tell them that while nihilism is fine for a boozy salon in {TOWN_NAME}, it's a bit much for men who must every day put their lives on the line.
{=4dIYUMkA}Donate the spoils of battle to the saint's shrine
{=4v8LpVb8}Send some men to fetch a doctor and medicine, accepting that it will delay your march
{=52l7VuWI}Tell her that Heaven expects her to bear her fate with dignity.
{=56hS9BRG}Admonish the {HIGH_TIER_TROOPS} for their indiscipline, even though they will be humiliated and may even desert

IL_39d4: ldstr          {=m35ezdZG}You don't need a bard to recount your heroic deeds
IL_39f8: ldstr          {=bJBLAnrc}Shower him with gold and tell him that he should feel free to embellish your story as he sees fit

IL_3a77: ldstr          {=HbOFGhTG}Tragic tales are always the most popular. Ensure the bard does not leave out the daemon who sits on your shoulder, your bouts of madness, and the witch who foretold your terrible but heroic death

IL_3ae2: ldstr          {=Tq4O8vic}One of your {KNIGHT} asks you for a favor. His daughter plans to marry a man from the back alleys of this town with a reputation as a no-good layabout. He has refused permission but asks you to do what you can to insure the two do not elope.

IL_3b00: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_3b06: ldstr          {=uppCchb0}Let them marry. Love must triumph over a father's pride

IL_3b83: ldstr          {=oQmuxCSk}Do your best to explain to the girl that marriages are affairs of the head, not of the heart, and she had better think of her future and that of her children and not elope.
IL_3bc5: ldstr          {=GMQROhTM}Order your troops to give the upstart a sound beating. Who does he think he is, the hero of some foolish romantic poem?

IL_3c15: ldstr          {=S2PV4Qeb}As you ride out of the village, an old man in rags comes up to you and grasps the halter of your horse. "You must tell me!" he barks. "What is the tale told by the sword?" Your men gather in to see if you will humor this seemingly mad hermit.

IL_3c46: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_3c4c: ldstr          {=2dW3cBQy}That steel is forged from iron, and long hard marches breed tough warriors.
IL_3c83: ldstr          {=PHo98vjr}That a sword is all you need, because if you own one, you can take whatever else you need from those without.
IL_3cba: ldstr          {=xhuGmF9r}That the force of the blade lies only in the hand that wields it.
IL_3cdd: ldstr          {=yMoBOgxx}"You tell me," you say, with a mad laugh, as you deal him a slice that draws blood.
IL_3d30: ldstr          {=GpUBP10Q}As you leave the village, a merchant who clearly wants your approval shouts out, "{LOCAL_KING} has slain his thousands, but {PLAYER} his tens of thousands!"

IL_3d61: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_3d67: ldstr          {=sxH5NHba}"I have, and it is but an appetite-whetter before the main meal."
IL_3dc6: ldstr          {=acBdTQxp}"All I have done has been in the service of {KING}. I am but his will made flesh."
IL_3e33: ldstr          {=naVH8uSO}"Any blood I have shed may have been necessary but I hope that Heaven will forgive me."
IL_3e56: ldstr          {=iR3ZuTSW}Acknowledge him by howling like an animal and swirling your weapon about, as mad behavior makes for good stories.

IL_3e97: ldstr          {=aqZyQ3Ca}A man, dressed as a nobleman's servant, approaches you. "I hear that you and {RIVALLORD.NAME} aren't on the best of terms. Well, what can you expect from a man who can't manage his own family? I was recently employed at his household, and know that his wife was unusually close to her groom... I can spread the word, if you make it worth my while."

IL_3eb4: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_3eba: ldstr          {=Gjd6nP29}You will not sully the good name of anyone with an obviously false rumor
IL_3ede: ldstr          {=jE9aKaYd}People will believe a noble's former servant. This man's favor is worth a purse of silver to you.
IL_3f71: ldstr          {=bZUMOAjU}Crack a few jokes to your men at {RIVALLORD.NAME}'s expense, but otherwise do nothing

IL_3fa8: ldstr          {=vaez5WXH}As you leave town, you see a much larger number of beggars gathered than you would expect. Some of their limps look unconvincing. Your reputation for compassion and generosity may have gotten around.

IL_3fd8: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_3fde: ldstr          {=DFIPsN1W}If they come to you in need, it is not for you to question them. Have your men distribute alms as usual.

IL_4041: ldstr          {=CKKIJZcB}Have some of your men boil up a soup. Keep a watchful eye on all the beggars, especially those who move too vigorously to the front of the line, and serve only those who seem genuinely too frail to work.
IL_40ab: ldstr          {=T1pwrLN9}Tell them that you are no chicken to be plucked. You will reward neither liars nor those who keep company with liars.

IL_40eb: ldstr          {=qBsa5KC5}As you leave town you come across an encampment of traveling entertainers. You see tattered but colorful tents, you hear wailing but enticing music, and smell the scent of cheap incense and meat that is probably slightly spoiled but spiced so that you would never notice. A group of women in some noble's thrown-away silks, their faces made up skillfully with charcoal and sheep's blood, beckon to your men. What do you do?

IL_411b: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_4121: ldstr          {=lPAC4x1e}Tell your men to steer clear of such dubious enticements
IL_4155: ldstr          {=xYuNxo3v}Let your men have some fun, but tell them to watch their purses and stay out of fights
IL_41aa: ldstr          {=mmlk2tXh}The fun is on you! Hurl a fistful of silver at the entertainers and tell them your men deserve nothing but the best
IL_420a: ldstr          {=lzK4PmYL}Rob the entertainers. No doubt their wealth is ill-gotten, and to whom will they complain?

IL_4262: ldstr          {=mZir8Ogn}As you prepare to leave, the village elder approaches you. There's a gang of four lads who are constantly picking fights with the other villagers, he says. Even their own families don't want them around for fear they'll end up killing someone and cause a blood feud. He begs you to take them into your ranks, where they can learn a bit of discipline.

IL_4292: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_4298: ldstr          {=ePstZcmu}Accept the recruits. The first chance you get, find fault with their gear and give them a sound thrashing, so they'll know to mend their ways.
IL_42e7: ldstr          {=Dogg1b9a}Take the recruits. Try not to be too hard on them at first, even though they'll probably corrode your party's discipline.
IL_4345: ldstr          {=EIbmlJRP}Tell the elder he'll need to find some other way to handle his troublemakers.

IL_4361: ldstr          {=FPnUWAj1}After the battle, one of your {TROOPS} from your party approaches you, dreamed of riding with your cavalry as a {NOBLE_TIER}. He has the money to buy his own horse, and he certainly distinguished himself in the fight. You know however that this will go down badly - with the high-born cavalry, who prefer to mingle with their own class, but probably even more so with his comrades, who will think he scorns them.

IL_437f: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_44c2: ldstr          {=uJYOhEx8}Commend him, but tell him to stick with his comrades

IL_4505: ldstr          {=BG8Ph5La}As you leave {VILLAGE_NAME}, a woman approaches you and grasps your horse's halter. Among your prisoners is her son, she says. You captured him when he was part of a gang of bandits, but she tells you tearfully that he is a good boy who fell in with bad company. She swears she'll ensure that he doesn't stray again from the correct path.

IL_4535: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_4590: ldstr          {=9yrWWbHF}Tell the woman that her son shall face the same penalties as any other bandit you caught
IL_45c5: ldstr          {=6sAI5uOm}Tell the village that they must pay the lad's ransom, so that he will know there is no profit in banditry

IL_464b: ldstr          {=VauaVUNS}You notice a footpath leading through your estate which could be quickly improved to be used by wagons and be a shortcut between the main trade roads. You could charge tolls and turn it into a turnpike, though the locals would resent the increased traffic and fees on their customary route.

IL_470c: ldstr          {=xxVE2bw1}Improve the road, but charge no tolls

IL_47db: ldstr          {=cRMxKTa8}Several freeholding farmers in your fief have fallen into debt through what appears to be a combination of bad luck and risky investments - a plough horse that died, a crop ruined by frost. They are unable to pay their taxes, and ask for a reprieve for several years.

IL_480c: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_48a6: ldstr          {=WHWokYrT}Call in a favor with a moneylender in town to reduce their debts so they can pay their taxes
IL_48f1: ldstr          {=3QobDImA}Help them get back on their feet, even if some will call say that you are too trusting

IL_495e: ldstr          {=lfJ6OHgX}The village has seen an unexpected rise in pregnancies. Some of your villagers ask your permission to hold a festival in honor of Agalea, protectress of motherhood. Agalea has never been recognized as a saint by the imperial Senate, and many consider her veneration to be a primitive Palaic holder. Her festivals tend to be rather raucous, befitting the theme of fertility, and also rather expensive. It would certainly set tongues wagging in the district. Do you grant permission?

IL_498f: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_4a89: ldstr          {=NWNIVZF0}Give the villagers a stern lecture on the importance of sound doctrine and lawful worship
IL_4b25: ldstr          {=J9BsFeSS}Tell the villagers to keep things discrete

IL_4b99: ldstr          {=2KaXj3Qa}The depredations of the {NEARBY_ENEMY_FACTION} has driven many farmers from their homes. Those who have land usually return to it, but many of the poorer are seeking a new place to live. You speak to a few encamped on the outskirts of your village. There is no land for them. They seem eager to work as tenants, but there is always a possibility of tensions with the more established village families.

IL_4bca: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_4c80: ldstr          {=U4UJn9X4}Let them stay. Tell both newcomers and longtime residents to get along, and hope for the best.
IL_4cf3: ldstr          {=o4aQ2UEL}Tell them to make their homes someplace else.

IL_4d21: ldstr          {=U4Ybz08z}A desperate band of nomads has arrived at your village, seeking a place to settle down. Their herds were ravaged by an epidemic, they say, and they are ready to take up farming or work as laborers. Otherwise, they must starve or give themselves to another tribe as servants. The villagers are skeptical. Nomads are too lazy to be farmers, they say, preferring horse theft and feuds.

IL_4d52: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_4e69: ldstr          {=jUlHTiSU}Agree with the villagers that nomads are more trouble than they are worth.

IL_4e97: ldstr          {=raLLq10c}Grazing land has grown scarce near {TOWN_OR_CASTLE_NAME}, and a heath between {POORER_VILLAGE} and {RICHER_VILLAGE}, covered with thistle and formerly of little value, has become a point of contention. {POORER_VILLAGE} claims that they have been taking goats there for generations, but {RICHER_VILLAGE} has produced a document showing legal title.

IL_4ec8: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_4ece: ldstr          {=cVzpV96W}The laws of the realm are clear: no matter how many years go by, the original owner retains the land unless it is legally sold or transferred.
IL_4f4c: ldstr          {=3zEtGAII}You agree with the ancient Palaic principle: the lands belong to the spirits of the earth, not to humans, and go to those who make the best use of them.
IL_5028: ldstr          {=YWZFOX4S}Let them know that your decision is for sale at a price

IL_50d7: ldstr          {=jGafCYMe}Villagers from your fief of {VILLAGE} have started going to a marsh on the road to {VILLAGE2} to gather reeds for baskets, supplementing their earnings. Hunters from {VILLAGE2}, owned by {LORD.NAME}, say they've been disturbing the local waterfowl. Neither of you has title to the marsh, but {VILLAGE2} says that its people started going there first. Your tenants say it's not their problem if they've figured out a better way to make use of the resources.

IL_50f5: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_519f: ldstr          {=0xiAZr96}Tell {NOBLE.NAME} that your people will get their reeds elsewhere and stop frightening off the game.

IL_521c: ldstr          {=2OQlwt7x}Villagers say that a wanderer has recently arrived and offered to teach their children to read. He is not only well-educated, but he has a gift for holding the attention of restless 10-year-olds. However, he seems to have spent time with one of the rebel bands that were common around here ten years back, and occasionally speaks of a coming reign of justice brought by Heaven, in a way that doesn't seem like one of his ironic jokes.

IL_524d: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_52cd: ldstr          {=zEPpgYaf}Reading won't help a farmboy plough, but might goad him to do foolish things that get him killed
IL_52f0: ldstr          {=3OerG5Ik}Take the teacher aside, and tell him the elder will pay him a handsome stipend that will stop abruptly if he breathes a word about politics or theology.

IL_5374: ldstr          {=eQz8b4TH}The village is buzzing with a poorly kept secret. Following a rare but fierce rainstorm in the dry hills, fishermen have begun to find small flakes of gold in a local stream. If word gets out, there will be a huge influx of fortune-seekers into the area. The gold will last a few months, and it's not clear how much of it will benefit the village or its owner.

IL_54cd: ldstr          {=cECwyvjY}Encourage the villagers to mine it stealthily, ensuring their cooperation by allowing them to keep it
IL_5551: ldstr          {=7q53TLg7}Wages of war and diseases

IL_5556: ldstr          {=FZXYHC7s}Between the wars and an epidemic, the villages near {FIEF_NAME} are experiencing a shortage of people, especially young men. Fields are going fallow for lack of hands to plough them, especially those cleared only in recent generations where the title is in dispute. As liege, you can redistribute this unused land, but you will need to find labor.

IL_5617: ldstr          {=8jCcqBSV}Distribute the land to some of your veterans as a reward for their service
IL_56b2: ldstr          {=QSEZfwVk}Distribute money to the region's farmers so they can hire agricultural laborers or provide attractive dowries for their daughters

IL_5765: ldstr          {=evcKUaab}An early thaw and a warm spring has ensured a bumper crop, which the prayers of the villagers and the efforts of the local cats have protected from rats and birds. Such bounties occur rarely. What will you do?

IL_58b6: ldstr          {=ZaBiC5XV}Go through your accounts to see who might owe you back taxes

IL_5911: ldstr          {=yXXbY1bb}You lie down for a well-deserved nap, but you slip into an uneasy dream. You are sailing on a wind-tossed sea. A wave crashes on your bow, sending spray across the decks. You look closely, and see that it is not water but blood sloshing around across your feet. You stare out into the sea, and the breakers take on the forms of men you have slain in battle.

IL_59bd: ldstr          {=B1cyEaQA}Dreams are but a temporary madness. Heaven does not speak to us in this way.

He offers to pay you 1000 denars, in addition to whatever extra you can make by selling your own wares once the prices rise.

IL_5b97: ldstr          {=aMMxVIpa}Erupt in anger for all to see, and curse {MERCHANT} for taking you for a base liar.
IL_5c1c: ldstr          {=UbZMlyk6}Take a pass on the matter.

IL_5c38: ldstr          {=H7Co1wqC}Two of your {NOBLE_TIER} have lately been causing a stir in the camp with their irreverent religious preaching. They propound that this world is a illusion, created by a being called the Demiurge for its own amusement, and humans are but game-pieces. You think this may be the Marcorionist doctrine, declared heretical by the imperial Senate some years ago. It is clearly disturbing your more traditional-minded troops and is probably also not good for your party's reputation.

IL_5c56: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_5c5c: ldstr          {=WyuxrGqC}Tell them, in a towering fury, that if they do not wish to be burned then they had best either leave your party or cease this sacrilege
IL_5cb9: ldstr          {=4WZ5CWm8}Take them aside and tell them that while nihilism is fine for a boozy salon in {TOWN_NAME}, it's a bit much for men who must every day put their lives on the line.

IL_5d15: ldstr          {=vzFoybv0}Tell your party that, if this is true, then men are free to choose their own purpose in this world - and anyone who stands with you should make his purpose to help those in need.
IL_5d48: ldstr          {=e07rQCcq}Tell the men that this is splendid news for brave men like themselves, as surely nothing would amuse the Demiurge more than a good fight.

IL_5dab: ldstr          {=vPNDzUAF}You strike up a conversation with a trader in town, who is desperate for news of the wars. When you tell him about the looting of {VILLAGE_NAME}, he makes a proposition. The price of grain will almost certainly rise, and he intends to buy up food now to sell it later when the hunger hits. He needs money, and he will sell you {OTHER_GOOD} at far below their market value - 1000 denars. He asks you also to keep this information to yourself.

IL_5dc9: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_5dcf: ldstr          {=aUui6FYp}All's fair in trade and war. You accept the deal.
IL_5e52: ldstr          {=2xvqOUJh}Tell him quietly that you will not profit off of the misery of others.
IL_5e75: ldstr          {=hnMUxRyt}Denounce him angrily in public as a food hoarder for all to hear, so that word gets around of your compassion and mercy.

IL_5ec8: ldstr          {=nyZpbVbv}Your men are very proud of their leader - perhaps too proud. Every time they go into town, they spread exaggerated tales of your recklessness in battle. You imagine that this could win you a few admiring recruits, but more and more you've caught a look that suggests fear or distrust, as though you're a wild animal or a demon.

IL_5ef8: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_5efe: ldstr          {=bbH4PqtD}Let the tales spread! Sanity and caution do not inspire legend
IL_5f5f: ldstr          {=Qbdym8vH}In a towering rage, tell your men that you will not tolerate lies of any sort.
IL_5f94: ldstr          {=EzpB6hJG}Try to play down the image of a madman by being as friendly as possible on your next visit to town.

IL_5fd4: ldstr          {=IxgJotDk}At first this siege gave your men a welcome respite from the hardships of the march, but now inactivity and boredom has started to take a toll. Even dice and gossip have lost their charms, and you're starting to see quarrels and lapses in discipline.

IL_6009: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_600f: ldstr          {=LUap9uP0}Drill your men for the upcoming assault, even though the ever-present risk of injury might put several out of commission when they're needed most.

IL_6048: ldstr          {=GTPPtara}March about the camp, searching for specks of rust on swords or sentries who aren't fully attentive to their watch. Give any violators hard, pointless tasks to teach them to keep their standards up.
IL_6095: ldstr          {=bp8kKb1A}Let the men enjoy their rest.

IL_60d3: ldstr          {=YCPF4qyz}You are approached by a pair of Skolderbroda. They are anxious to fight for you and ask only that you pay them a token sum. They say you that a warlord like you deserves the services of men such as themselves - praise to you, but a slight to the rest of your party. One of your troops tells you that he's sure that these men must have broken their vows to their company, or why else would they be so eager to join you?

IL_6103: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_6109: ldstr          {=Kqr9pVCU}Take them into your company. Your troops will need to bear any insult.
IL_615c: ldstr          {=78VrrDRM}Tell them that you believe them to be oathbreakers, and as such have no place in your ranks.
IL_617f: ldstr          {=1b9oYu6v}Tell them they can join you and be as arrogant as they like - so long as they beat one of your men in a duel to first blood.

IL_620b: ldstr          {=K8DJmY4L}Several of your {TROOP_TYPE} have an idea for the next battle. They suggest that they be hidden in a supply wagon and left for the enemy to discover and drag into camp, whereupon they will leap out and wreak havoc. They are very proud of their scheme, even though you can think of half a dozen reasons it won't work.

IL_6228: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_622e: ldstr          {=X68PZrYv}Tell them that every people in Calradia has its own legend about warriors concealed in unlikely places, and you can't imagine them getting away with it.
IL_6264: ldstr          {=Gsazqfhj}Let them test their plan. Buy a hide, sew the men into it with their weapons, and gather the company to watch in amusement as they struggle to free themselves.
IL_62c9: ldstr          {=YhxsQjGM}Nod quickly as though you weren't really listening and move on to some other task.

IL_62f7: ldstr          {=42bGMh4X}Your men were not expecting to spend so much time in the desert. They complain that baggage that they might gladly carry themselves in normal times becomes a crushing burden when the blazing sun is high in the sky. They have located a number of pack animals in the markets and ask you to buy them to lighten their own loads.

IL_6327: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_632d: ldstr          {=ACzeec4e}Agree to purchase the camels.
IL_63c3: ldstr          {=uD8su80f}Tell them that you need the money for other purposes.

IL_63f4: ldstr          {=3IphvZTK}In your absence, several families in your district have been hard at work draining a marsh and turning it into a field. The survey records in your treasury however indicate clearly that the marsh is part of your domain. They almost certainly did not know this, but you are entitled to claim the field or charge them for working it.

IL_6429: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_6491: ldstr          {=j0HmgDOA}Maintain your claim to the land, but allow the farmers to make use of it for only a token rent.
IL_651c: ldstr          {=xcPJPtaT}Demand the land for yourself.

IL_65b0: ldstr          {=3eOOT66E}One of your tenants has a proposal for you. He proposes to dig a channel known as a qanah into a hillside, where the water table is high, which will allow him to flood some low-lying ground and turn it into an oasis garden. The barren hillside is your property, though at present it yields no income of any kind.

IL_65e5: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_663b: ldstr          {=iB2g7XBt}Insist he purchase the hillside from your at market rate.
IL_66b4: ldstr          {=P8W5OQB9}Wait until he digs the channel and clears the fields, then charge him heavily to use the water without which his effort will be for nothing.

IL_674d: ldstr          {=QEP3ntdb}Merchants are savvy to most attempts to pass off most types of shoddy goods as top quality, but one of your {TROOP.NAME} knows a few tricks that aren't in the usual rogue's repetoire. He suggests buying a selection of spices from the market, then sprinkling a bit of pomegranate rind in with the saffron, some cassia bark with the cinnamon, and a lead compound known as litharge with the pepper.

IL_676b: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_6771: ldstr          {=lrysxcAE}A bit of lead never hurt anyone! Try them all, and split the profits with your {TROOP.NAME}.
IL_6828: ldstr          {=tDK8b1J8}You vaguely recall hearing that lead might be poisonous, but you'll try the others.
IL_68bf: ldstr          {=MfbK2Sqa}Tell your man to save his ingenuity for battle, not trade.
IL_68f4: ldstr          {=a5gLRsa4}Thank your man bruskly and try his trick, but pay him nothing.

IL_6980: ldstr          {=a939QfLJ}As you leave {TOWN_NAME}, a young woman throws herself in front of your horse. She raises her face to the sky, tears at her hair, and wails that her young husband signed up to fight for you and was slain in battle. "You took him from me!" she screams. It is not clear what she wants.

IL_69b0: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_69b6: ldstr          {=8uabQDxp}Tell her, as soberly as you can, that her husband gave his life for a noble cause. Hand her a purse of 100 denars, and tell her that you are sure that he would be happy if she marries again, as long as he remains in her memory.

IL_6a04: ldstr          {=kZJvgtE3}Dismount, burst into tears, take her hands in yours and tell her that every life lost in your service tears at your heart, and that you want nothing more but for these wars to end.
IL_6a3d: ldstr          {=52l7VuWI}Tell her that Heaven expects her to bear her fate with dignity.
IL_6a60: ldstr          {=Sz28bZOI}Have your purser speak to her at length about what she might need, as you keep your distance.

IL_6ab1: ldstr          {=PqzLYt6i}Some time recently - you're not sure exactly when - your men started a new post-battle tradition - going about the field collecting grisly trophies from slain enemies. Now you can't help noticing these prizes dangling from their belts or the halters of their horses.

IL_6ae2: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_6ae8: ldstr          {=1zsWhG2N}Tell your men as best you can that, while you respect their spirit, this will frighten local farmers who don't understand warriors' ways.
IL_6b2e: ldstr          {=VHlwd8na}Take a lively interest in each of these ornaments, asking your men at which battle and from which fallen foe they were taken.
IL_6bbe: ldstr          {=xoH5LaY0}Harangue your men for their barbarism, tell them to honor rather than mock their fallen foes.

IL_6c59: ldstr          {=YAnTtrLs}Your reputation as a skilled trader generally does you good, but there is always a downside. When you arrive in {TOWN}, the market inspector descends from his tower to present you with a list of fees that you supposedly accumulated over the years, based on decrees that go back several centuries. The decrees may be genuine, but in all your talk with merchants, you never heard of anyone ever paying them.

IL_6c8e: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_6c94: ldstr          {=RPyFwR6I}Erupt in fury, telling the inspector that there is no way you will be fleeced in this way, legally or illegally.
IL_6d09: ldstr          {=vzA2ZJog}Pay, but say for all to hear that selective application of obscure laws is little better than theft.
IL_6d57: ldstr          {=ogP9E5Hx}Reason with the inspector over a splendid dinner and an amphora of the finest wine that is of course on you.
IL_6db4: ldstr          {=9aYLFpC9}Just hand over the money to make the problem go away.

IL_6e0c: ldstr          {=XQU3Tobe}Knowing your reputation as a trader, two merchants in {TOWN_NAME} are asking you to arbitrate a dispute between them. The two had drawn up a contract wherein each partner had a half-share in an incoming shipment of wine. When it arrived, however, the sea captain demanded twice the price. The wealthier of the two partners was at the docks. He took the initiative and purchased the goods, deciding to take a loss for the sake of his reputation as a reliable supplier to the local taverns, but the second is poorer and wants out of the deal.

IL_6e41: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_6e47: ldstr          {=nbshAaHo}The letter of the contract would favor the wealthier partner. Merchants should be careful what they sign.
IL_6e8d: ldstr          {=bsC5zEoI}Never mind the letter of the contract, the reasonable, decent move for the richer merchant would have been to consult with his partner.
IL_6ed3: ldstr          {=Ib04QQJY}Tell them that the whole thing gives you a headache.
IL_6ee4: ldstr          {=0ZP5fDBX}Let the wealthier merchant know that your decision is for sale.

IL_6f3f: ldstr          {=fhjyEgld}Your troops are taking a bit longer than usual to get ready, and you've had time to relax a bit and watch goings-on at the market. One commodity vendor in particular has caught your attention. He always uses one set of weights for the sacks that he is buying from local farmers, and another for goods that he sells. You have little doubt that one or both of these sets is a false measure, allowing him to defraud his customers.

IL_6f70: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_6f88: ldstr          {=Uidhqph1}Denounce the merchant loudly, even if you run the risk of making enemies among the town elite.

IL_6fe1: ldstr          {=MGfXReQC}Walk up to the merchant, and insist he use the lighter weights to sell you one measure of his goods. Then come back later and return them, insisting he use the heavier weights.

IL_704e: ldstr          {=1jAyaivZ}As you pass through the village streets, a dog dashes out from among some spectators and bites at the heels of one of your {CAVALRYMAN}'s horses, panicking it. IL_706b: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)

IL_70c1: ldstr          {=5HsJkbZz}You brought your men into their village, and you must take responsibility.
IL_710e: ldstr          {=te1A19Xe}Tell your {CAVALRYMAN} that he can sort it out.

IL_7147: ldstr          {=EbNZg7jp}In hot climes, often the most vulnerable part of a fortress is its water supply. Most depend on wells but those can run dry. After days spent in front of {FORTRESS_NAME}, you've caught glimpses of the defenders slipping into the hills. You explore where they've gone, and eventually you come across a rudimentary cistern. You suspect that they must be refreshing their water here.

IL_717c: call           TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.RegisterIncident(System.String, System.String, System.String, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentTrigger, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.IncidentsCampaignBehaviour+IncidentType, TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignTime, System.Func<TaleWorlds.Localization.TextObject, System.Boolean>)
IL_7182: ldstr          {=57VuY9ln}Poison it! Some women and children of {FORTRESS_NAME} may well perish along with the defenders, but such is war.

IL_723a: ldstr          {=bGaD3LoG}The best blows are struck not to the body but to the spirit. Let the defenders know you found it by diverting it to a pool where your men can bathe on the hottest, thirstiest days of the siege.
IL_7299: ldstr          {=iiwhVNBb}You respect the defenders' cunning. Simply observe how they slip out of the fortress, by ropes or hidden gates, and learn from it.

IL_72ca: ldstr          {=0DSopB7F}After observing the terrain around {FORTRESS_NAME}, you think conditions might be appropriate for mining - digging a tunnel under a wall, then collapsing it. This can open a breach but is time-consuming and risky. If you encounter rock underground, you may find all your efforts go to waste. If the ground is too soft, the tunnel may collapse and bury your men. Most troops are reluctant to spend time in dark, confined tunnels unless they are paid extra, or forced.

IL_74f3: ldstr          {=lCumAw9j}Rely on the usual methods

IL_769f: ldstr          {=wJ3Nh230}A breach is not worth the losses.
